lots.what_it_is: Van Diemens Land parchment indenture, 1835: mortgage by William Thomas and Mary Maria Stocker to Rolla O'Ferrall (Derwent Hotel, per catalogue), with a related second indenture involving Gamaliel Butler and a receipt endorsement
lots.guide_summary: No comparable entries survive: the researcher found none (web search budget exhausted) and my own search attempt was refused for the same reason; a curl fallback to Mojeek returned HTTP 403. 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking. No currency conversion used.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0 (Gowans premium 19.8%, all-in = hammer x 1.198, would apply if evidence existed). Pickup from 37 Main Road, Moonah, inbound freight $0.
lots.confidence_reason: Identification is clear from the photos (names and the sum are legible), but there is not a single verified price of any kind, so value rests on judgement only.
lots.dropped_entries: None to drop: the researcher supplied no entries.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photos confirm the researcher. Photo 2/3/4: engrossed 'This Indenture' heading, text naming William Thomas Stocker and Mary Maria Stocker and Rolla O'Ferrall, principal sum of One Thousand Five Hundred pounds, signed Wm Stocker (and Wm T Stocker) with red wax seals and a Rolla O'Ferrall signature. The top edges are scalloped (a genuinely indented deed). Photo 1 crop: 'Signed Sealed and Delivered' attestations, including one for Mary Maria Stocker. Photo 5 crop: a receipt acknowledging payment to Gamaliel Butler of One Thousand Seven hundred and eighty nine pounds three shillings and sixpence, noted '1789-3-6', witnessed by a Harris, signed by O'Ferrall. Photo 6: second indenture with two seals. The Derwent Hotel name comes from the catalogue title; I did not find it in the legible text.
lots.condition: Several parchment sheets, heavy fold lines, some grubbiness and staining, cockled edges; wax seals appear present and largely intact; text legible.
lots.question_for_gowans: How many separate documents/membranes are in the lot, are all seals intact, and where in the text is the Derwent Hotel named (is the property description legible)?
lots.score_reason: Early (1835) named Hobart mortgage deeds with seals attract Tasmanian collectors and typically sell in the low hundreds, but this is judgement, not verified evidence; scored mid-range for that reason.
